claim: For each of Elsenhans--Jahnel's two Example 4.7 plane quartics \(C_{F,5}\) and \(C_{F,-5}\) over \(\mathbb Q\), where \(F(T)=T^6-24T^5+152T^4-340T^3+335T^2-150T+25\), the Galois action on the \(63\) nonzero classes of \(J(C)[2]\) has orbit sizes \(1,6,16,16,24\). Hence \(J(C)(\mathbb Q)[2]\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\), so the distinguished Steiner hexad constructed in the source is the unique Galois-invariant Steiner hexad. The singleton orbit is the class defining that distinguished hexad. The conclusion applies to both signs because the source proves that their bitangent Galois images are conjugate in \(\operatorname{Sp}_6(\mathbb F_2)\).
integrity: The finite-group calculation is exhaustive and reproducible from the attached exact verifier; literature claims are separated from the new orbit computation.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns only the two explicit quartics of Example 4.7 and only their rational two-torsion and associated Steiner-hexad orbit structure.
No claim is made about odd-primary torsion, the full group \(J(C)(\mathbb Q)\), or quartics outside these examples.
An older or unindexed theta-characteristic computation could in principle contain an equivalent \(63\)-point orbit calculation.
title: Example 4.7 has a unique rational Steiner hexad
